title: A region bounded by a logarithm, a line and the x-axis

stimulus.title: The region <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> bounded by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4 - x</annotation></semantics></math> and the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis

parts.label: a

rubric.point: Integral: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{d} \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.074</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = \ln c \approx 1.074</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^c \ln x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>c</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_c^4 (4 - x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.926</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c \approx 2.926</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: either form, with correct limits found from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x = 4 - x</annotation></semantics></math>

one integral in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> from 1 to 4 of a single integrand does not earn this point

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln x = 4 - x</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2.926271</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = c = 2.926271</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \ln c</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4 - c</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.073729</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.073729</annotation></semantics></math>. In <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>, each horizontal strip runs from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e^y</annotation></semantics></math> (left) to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4 - y</annotation></semantics></math> (right). Area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_0^{d} \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.792</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.792</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid generated when RR is revolved about the vertical line x=5x = 5.

rubric.point: Integrand: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(5 - e^y\right)^2 - \left(5 - (4 - y)\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(5 - e^y\right)^2 - (1 + y)^2</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: outer radius <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 - e^y</annotation></semantics></math> (to the far, left edge), inner radius <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + y</annotation></semantics></math> (to the line)

radii in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, or the square of the difference, do not earn this point

parts.sample: Horizontal washers for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le y \le d</annotation></semantics></math>. The axis <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 5</annotation></semantics></math> is to the right of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>, so the far edge is the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e^y</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\text{out}} = 5 - e^y</annotation></semantics></math>, and the near edge is the line <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4 - y</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>in</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 5 - (4 - y)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 + y</annotation></semantics></math>. Volume <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \pi\int_0^{d} \left[\left(5 - e^y\right)^2 - (1 + y)^2\right]\,dy</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>27.403</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 27.403</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Region RR is the base of a solid. For this solid, each cross section perpendicular to the xx-axis is a semicircle whose diameter lies in RR. Find the volume of the solid.

rubric.point: Setup: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>c</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{8}\left[\int_1^c (\ln x)^2\,dx + \int_c^4 (4 - x)^2\,dx\right]</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: the area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\pi\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, c]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = 4 - x</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[c, 4]</annotation></semantics></math>

the integral must be split at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = c</annotation></semantics></math>; a radius of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> instead of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{s}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> does not earn this point

parts.sample: Across <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, the diameter is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \le x \le c</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = 4 - x</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c \le x \le 4</annotation></semantics></math>. A semicircle of diameter <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> has area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>8</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\pi\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{\pi}{8}s^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Volume <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>c</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>c</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\pi}{8}\left[\int_1^c (\ln x)^2\,dx + \int_c^4 (4 - x)^2\,dx\right]</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.532</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.532</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The horizontal line y=ky = k divides RR into two regions of equal area. Write, but do not solve, an equation involving one or more integrals whose solution gives kk.

rubric.point: An integral of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - y - e^y</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dy</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> as a limit
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^k \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_k^{d} \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^k \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.792</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}(1.792)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^k \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>d</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int_k^{d} \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Below the line <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = k</annotation></semantics></math> the area of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^k \left(4 - y - e^y\right)\,dy</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> solves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^k \left(4 -
